summary: @servicetitan/anvil-react 0.11.4 ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs", which runs on npm install before any user interaction. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (_0xNNNN identifiers, per-function string dictionaries) and downloads the Bun runtime binary (bun-v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (shuffled string array with a WV8StW rotator, ~1500-entry mixed dictionary n7gIxM, indirect character-decoder hc1jfK9, hex-renamed identifiers) whose contents cannot be inspected as-shipped. Executing the payload under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime bypasses Node-based scanners and hooks. The rest of the tarball is a normal @servicetitan React design-system library (Alert, Button, Calendar, Dialog components re-exported from dist/ui-react.cjs); the preinstall dropper and math_init.js are unrelated to that UI purpose, consistent with a hijacked or malicious release published under the @servicetitan scope. The math_init.js payload is also directly executable by any pre-existing bun on the installer's PATH.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
